newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Nafta Polska privatisation data in month.
newsitem.headline: Polish Nafta Polska privatisation data in month.

text.p: Polish oil holding Nafta Polska SA will issue information for investors about its privatisation within a month despite delays in restructuring the CPN SA fuel distribution chain, the holding's deputy president said.
Marek Foltynowicz told Reuters on Wednesday Nafta Polska planned to keep to its restructuring scheme which envisages the joint privatisation of the country's refineries and CPN.
"Within a month we will present the privatisation memorandum...and Nafta Polska has not changed its approach to restructuring the oil sector," Foltynowicz said.
He said CPN would likely give Nafta Polska a planned 25.5 percent stake by the end of the first quarter of 1997. It was originally expected to hand over the shares by the end of 1996.

At the weekend the state-owned CPN signed a $400 million deal with Israel's Dor Energy to build 400 stations in Poland, casting some doubt over its willingness to participate in the country's oil-sector restructuring scheme.

Under the government's privatisation scheme the state-owned Nafta Polska will offer between 20 and 30 percent of shares in the country's two major refineries to potential strategic investors, possibly this year.
CPN is also required to grant a minority stake to the two refineries, giving the investors access to CPN's lucrative distribution chain of nearly 1,400 of Poland's 4,600 filling stations.
The buyers would be allowed to increase their stakes in the refineries to majority holdings after investing in the modernisation of the companies.
After several years Nafta Polska would itself be privatised, most likely through a public share issue, with the state retaining a majority stake.
